entry: Spiritual, heavenly or supernatural being, often a messenger between God and humanity. Angels are often depicted as humanoid with bird-like wings, halos and divine light, though sometimes as frightening or inhuman. Other roles include guardian angels and servants of God. Revelation-based belief systems require angels to bridge the gap between the earthly and the transcendent realm. [[Abrahamic religions]] describe angelic hierarchies that vary by religion and sect. Named angels include [[Gabriel]] and [[Michael (archangel)|Michael]], and ranks include seraph and archangel. Malevolent angels, called fallen angels, are often believed to have been expelled from [[Heaven]], and in many such religions the [[Devil|devil]] is identified with them. The English word derives from [[Old English]] engel and Old French angele, from Late Latin angelus, from Late Greek ángelos, meaning “messenger.”

American Marxist feminist political activist, philosopher and academic. A member of the Communist Party USA until 1991, she ran for vice president on its ticket in 1980 and 1984. Hired by the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1969, she was fired by the regents over her party membership; after a court ruled the firing illegal, the university dismissed her for inflammatory language. In 1970 guns belonging to her were used in an armed courtroom takeover in Marin County, California, which killed four people. She was held for more than a year before being acquitted of all charges, including conspiracy to murder, in 1972.

Irish-British and American actress and singer. Lansbury made films for [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] in the 1940s, then turned increasingly to the stage, winning her first Tony Award for the Broadway musical *Mame* (1966). Her television role as the sleuth Jessica Fletcher in *Murder, She Wrote* (1984–1996) brought her worldwide fame. Her accolades include six Tony Awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award, six Golden Globe Awards and the Academy Honorary Award, and she received nominations for three Academy Awards. In 2014 she was made a dame by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]].

German politician, chancellor of Germany 2005–2021. Merkel was the only woman and the only former East German to hold the office. After a doctorate in quantum chemistry and work as a research scientist, she entered politics in the wake of the [[Revolutions of 1989]] and became a protégée of [[Helmut Kohl]]. She led the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) from 2000 to 2018. As chancellor she managed the [[2008 financial crisis]] and the euro area crisis, and her *Energiewende* program supported renewable energy while phasing out [[Nuclear power|nuclear power]] in Germany. In foreign policy she emphasized cooperation within the [[European Union]] and [[NATO]], but her close relations with [[Russia]], including the Nord Stream 2 pipelines, drew increasing scrutiny after Russia's 2022 invasion of [[Ukraine]]. She did not seek a fifth term in 2021.

American actress, filmmaker and humanitarian. Jolie won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for *Girl, Interrupted* (1999) and became a leading lady with *Lara Croft: Tomb Raider* (2001). Her later films include the action film *Salt* (2010) and the fantasy film *Maleficent* (2014). She directed the war dramas *In the Land of Blood and Honey* (2011) and *Unbroken* (2014). She served as a special envoy for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and undertook field missions to refugee camps and war zones.

Temple complex in Siem Reap, [[Cambodia]], originally built as a Hindu temple dedicated to [[Vishnu]]. It is the largest religious complex in the world, on a site measuring 162.6 hectares (1.6 km²; 401.8 acres). Commissioned by [[Suryavarman II]] (ruled 1113–c. 1150) in the capital of the [[Khmer Empire]], it is generally considered to have been intended as his mausoleum. Its layout is commonly interpreted as a representation of Mount Meru, with a broad moat and three progressively elevated galleries rising toward a central quincunx of towers. From the late 13th century it became a Buddhist temple, and it remains an active Buddhist monastery. Restoration was coordinated by the International Coordinating Committee for the Safeguarding and Development of the Historic Site of Angkor, established in 1993 under [[UNESCO]]. The Angkor area became a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1992, and the temple attracts more than 2.5 million visitors every year.

Ray-finned fish of the order Lophiiformes, with a dorsal fin ray modified into a lure for prey. The order contains over 400 species of marine fish, found from tropical seas to polar regions, in both shallow water and the deep sea. Many species are benthic, using enlarged pectoral or pelvic fins to rest on or move across the seabed, while deep-sea anglerfish lack pelvic fins and are pelagic. Sexual dimorphism is sometimes extremely pronounced: females may be several orders of magnitude larger in mass than males. In deep-sea species the male attaches to the much larger female and sometimes fuses with her, a phenomenon known as [[Parasitism|sexual parasitism]]. Lophiid anglerfish, marketed as monkfish or goosefish, are fished commercially for their highly valued meat.

Western Christian tradition that developed from the [[Church of England]] after the English Reformation. The Anglican Communion, the world's third-largest Christian communion, has around 110 million adherents as of 2025. The Church of England declared independence from the [[Holy See]] through the Act of Supremacy in 1534, a separation later consolidated by the Elizabethan Religious Settlement. It retained apostolic succession, and its mid-16th-century formularies correspond closely to those of historical [[Protestantism]]. The Book of Common Prayer, unique to Anglicanism, is acknowledged as a principal tie binding the communion. After the American Revolution, Anglican congregations in the United States and British North America became autonomous churches, a model that spread with the [[British Empire]]. The archbishop of Canterbury is recognized as the communion's primus inter pares. In 2020 there were 63,556,000 adherents in Africa, the center of the communion having shifted to the Global South.

Fishing technique using a hook attached to a line, usually handled with a rod. The name derives from [[Old English]] angol, meaning “hook.” The angler casts a baited hook, or a lure with several hooks, into the water and waits for a fish to bite; a float, bell or quiver tip signals the strike. The angler then sets the hook, tires the fish and lands it, often with a net. Angling is the principal method of recreational fishing, though commercial fisheries use related methods such as longlining and trolling. Many regions require a fishing license and impose size limits, and catch-and-release is increasingly practiced to conserve stocks. Popular game fish include [[Tuna]] and grouper in saltwater, and [[Trout]] and [[Salmon]] in freshwater. Angling differs from snagging, which uses large grappling hooks that pierce the fish externally.

Series of four conflicts between the Dutch Republic and the states of England and Great Britain, 1652–1784. The first three wars, in the second half of the 17th century, arose from tensions over trade and colonial expansion, and almost all the battles were naval engagements. England won the first war, while the Dutch were successful in the second and third. By the fourth war the [[Royal Navy]] had become the most powerful maritime force in the world, and the Dutch navy had fallen to fourth position behind the French and Spanish navies, making the fourth war a profound humiliation for the Dutch. During the [[Napoleonic Wars|French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars]], intermittent conflict continued, and Britain captured most of the Dutch colonial empire and destroyed much of the Dutch navy.

Early medieval cultural group speaking Old English and inhabiting much of what is now England and south-eastern Scotland. Its members traced their origins to Germanic settlers who became one of the most important cultural groups in Britain by the 5th century. The Anglo-Saxon period is usually dated from about 450 to the [[Norman Conquest]] in 1066. By the 8th century an Anglo-Saxon identity called *Englisc* had developed from the interaction of the settlers with the existing Romano-British culture. By 1066 most inhabitants of what is now England spoke [[Old English]] and were considered English. Late Anglo-Saxon structures and language are the direct predecessors of the high medieval [[Kingdom of England]] and [[Middle English]]. Although less than 26% of modern English words derive from Old English, these include over 80% of everyday words. The historian [[Bede]] gave the earliest detailed account of their origins.

British colonial war against the Zulu Kingdom in present-day [[South Africa]], fought from January to early July 1879. The Zulu Kingdom had grown into a regional power under [[Shaka]] in the 1810s, and the war was part of British plans to consolidate control over southern Africa. Sir Bartle Frere, the British High Commissioner for Southern Africa, sent an ultimatum to King Cetshwayo on 11 December 1878, and after its rejection Lord Chelmsford invaded Zululand. The Zulu won the Battle of Isandlwana, but a small British garrison held Rorke's Drift against a much larger attack. The British gained the upper hand at Kambula and took the Zulu capital of Ulundi. The Zulu Kingdom was made a protectorate of the [[British Empire]] and was annexed in 1887.

Country on the western coast of Southern Africa (pop., 2024: 36.6 million). It is the second-largest Portuguese-speaking country after [[Brazil]] in both area and population, and its capital is [[Luanda]]. The [[Kingdom of Kongo]] was the dominant state in the region from the 14th century, and Portuguese colonization of the coast began in the 16th century. Independence from [[Portugal]] in 1975 was followed by a civil war that lasted until 2002. Since then Angola has been a relatively stable constitutional republic with one of the world's fastest-growing economies, though wealth is concentrated among a small part of the population and life expectancy is among the lowest in the world. Petroleum drives approximately 50% of GDP and more than 90% of exports. Angola is a member of the [[United Nations]] and the [[African Union]].

Civil war in [[Angola]] from 1975 to 2002, fought between rival former anti-colonial movements. The communist People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) fought the anti-communist National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA). The National Front for the Liberation of Angola (FNLA) played almost no role after the initial phase. Backed by [[Cuba]] and the [[Soviet Union]], the MPLA won the initial conventional fighting, ousted the FNLA from [[Luanda]] and became the de facto government. UNITA, supported by the United States and South Africa, continued irregular warfare from its base in the east and south. Major fighting occurred in three periods: 1975 to 1991, 1992 to 1994, and 1998 to 2002. By 2002, between 500,000 and 800,000 people had died and over one million had been internally displaced. The war is widely considered a [[Cold War]] proxy conflict. [[Land mine|Land mines]] continue to cause civilian casualties.

Unit of length equal to 10⁻¹⁰ meter, or 0.1 nanometre. It is named after the Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström. The angstrom is used to express the sizes of [[Atom|atoms]] and [[Molecule|molecules]], the lengths of chemical bonds and the wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation; visible light has wavelengths in the range of 4000–7000 Å. Spectroscopists adopted it in the late 19th century, and in 1960 the meter was redefined so that the angstrom again equaled 10⁻¹⁰ meter. Never part of the [[International System of Units]], it has increasingly been replaced by the nanometre.

British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean, north of [[Saint Martin (island)|Saint Martin]] and one of the most northerly of the Leeward Islands. The main island is about 16 miles (26 kilometers) long, and the total land area of the territory is 35 square miles (91 km²). It had a population of approximately 15,753 in 2021; the capital is The Valley. Traditional accounts date English colonization from 1650, when settlers arrived from [[Saint Kitts and Nevis|Saint Kitts]]. It was returned to English control under the Treaty of Breda in 1667, and in 1967 residents voted overwhelmingly for secession from the Saint Kitts government.

Rotational analogue of linear momentum and a conserved physical quantity. Angular momentum has both direction and magnitude, and for a system with zero net external torque the total angular momentum is constant. Bicycles, flying discs, rifled bullets and [[Gyroscope|gyroscopes]] owe useful properties to its conservation, which is also why hurricanes form spirals and [[Neutron star|neutron stars]] rotate rapidly. For a point particle it is the cross product of position and linear momentum, so it depends on the chosen origin. [[Torque]] is the rate of change of angular momentum, analogous to force. The orbital angular momentum of the [[Earth]] with respect to the [[Sun]] is about 2.66 × 10⁴⁰ J⋅s, while its rotational angular momentum is about 7.05 × 10³³ J⋅s. In [[Quantum mechanics|quantum mechanics]], angular momentum is represented by operators, and its magnitude and projections are quantized. Its conservation follows from the rotational symmetry of space, through [[Noether's theorem]].

Indian actor and film producer who works mainly in Hindi cinema. Kapoor made his breakthrough in the 1980s with films including *Mr. India* (1987) and *Tezaab* (1988). Over a career of more than 40 years he has appeared in more than 100 films. His first international film role was in [[Danny Boyle|Danny Boyle's]] *Slumdog Millionaire* (2008). He has received two National Film Awards and seven Filmfare Awards. Kapoor has also starred in Indian television remakes, including *24* (2013–2016) and *The Night Manager* (2023).

Oral and anal sex act in which one person stimulates the anus of another using the tongue or lips. Also called rimming. The anus has a relatively high concentration of nerve endings, and the recipient may receive pleasure from the stimulation. The act may be practiced for its own sake, before anal penetration, or as part of foreplay. It carries a risk of infection through the fecal–oral route, including viral [[Hepatitis C|hepatitis]] and [[Escherichia coli|E. coli]] infections and other [[Sexually transmitted infection|sexually transmitted infections]]. Safer-sex precautions focus on [[Hygiene|hygiene]], STI testing and dental dams.

Satirical allegorical novella by [[George Orwell]], first published in England on August 17, 1945. The animals of Manor Farm rebel against their owner and set out to create an egalitarian society. The rebellion is betrayed as the pigs take control, and the farm ends in a dystopian state nearly identical to what it had been before. Orwell wrote the book as a satire against [[Joseph Stalin]], inspired by the [[Russian Revolution]] and the Stalinist era of the [[Soviet Union]]. Rejected by several publishers during the wartime alliance with the Soviet Union, it became a commercial success as the [[Cold War]] began. It won a Retrospective Hugo Award in 1996.

General appearance of an animal, resulting from light reflected or emitted by its surfaces. Coloration has evolved for several reasons. [[Camouflage]] keeps an animal hidden, color can advertise cleaning services or signal sexual status, and mimicry takes advantage of the warning coloration of other species. Some animals use flashes of color to startle predators, and pigments in the skin protect against sunburn. Animals produce color directly through [[Pigment|pigment]] or indirectly through chromatophores, whose pigment can shift under hormonal or neuronal control. Microscopic structures in the scales, bristles or feathers of many butterflies and birds produce iridescent colors. In the [[Peafowl]], the male has strong patterns and conspicuous colors, while the female is far less visible. [[Squid]] and some deep-sea fish can produce light.

Methods by which animals move from one place to another. Some locomotion is self-propelled, such as running, swimming, jumping, flying, hopping, soaring and gliding. Passive locomotion relies on the environment or other animals, as in sailing by some [[Jellyfish|jellyfish]], kiting by [[Spider|spiders]], or riding on other animals. Animals move to find food, mates or suitable habitat, or to escape predators, and [[Natural selection]] has shaped their methods. Migratory animals such as the Arctic tern typically use locomotion that costs little energy per unit distance, while animals that must escape predators often use costly but very fast movement. In water, a body less dense than water relies on [[Buoyancy|buoyancy]], and most fish generate thrust by oscillating the body. [[Cephalopod|Cephalopods]] travel fast by jet propulsion. On the seabed, [[Echinoderm|echinoderms]] move with tube feet, while crabs typically walk sideways.

Relatively long-distance movement of animals, usually on a seasonal basis. It is the most common form of migration in ecology and occurs in birds, mammals, fish, reptiles, amphibians, insects and crustaceans. Causes include local climate, food availability, season and mating. To count as true migration, the movement must be an annual or seasonal occurrence, or a major habitat change in an animal's life. Examples include Northern Hemisphere birds flying south for winter, [[Wildebeest|wildebeest]] moving annually to seasonal grazing, and young [[Salmon|Atlantic salmon]] leaving the river of their birth. Migration may be obligate, when all individuals migrate, or facultative. Birds may use a [[Circadian rhythm|circadian rhythm]] together with annual clocks to orient in time and space. Before its causes were understood, folklore held that [[Goose|barnacle geese]] grew from goose barnacles.

Philosophy holding that many or all sentient animals have moral worth independent of their utility to humans. Advocates argue that animals' basic interests, such as avoiding [[Suffering|suffering]], deserve the same consideration as similar human interests. In a narrower sense, animal rights are fundamental rights to life, liberty and freedom from torture that may not be overridden by aggregate welfare. Many advocates oppose assigning moral value on the basis of species membership alone. Some legal scholars support extending basic legal rights and personhood to nonhuman animals, most often great apes; [[Argentina]] granted captive orangutans basic human rights in 2014. Critics such as Roger Scruton argue that only humans have duties, and therefore only humans have rights. Utilitarian critics argue that animals may be used as resources so long as there is no unnecessary suffering.

Sexual behavior of non-human animals, which takes many forms, including within the same species. Common mating systems include monogamy, polygyny, polyandry, [[Polygamy|polygamy]] and [[Promiscuity|promiscuity]]. For most non-human mammals, mating occurs at oestrus, the most fertile period of the female's reproductive cycle. Non-reproductive sexual behavior has been recorded in over 1,500 species, including [[Bonobo|bonobos]] and [[Dolphin|dolphins]], and it may help maintain social bonds. Historically it was assumed that animal sexuality was simply instinctive, but a range of species masturbate, and some use objects as tools to do so.
